title: material
body:
## material

Creates a Blender material whose Principled BSDF shader inputs are set from the options: colour drives Base Color and Alpha, and the other options drive Roughness, Metallic, IOR, Transmission Weight, Coat Weight, Coat Roughness, Emission Color and Emission Strength. It produces a material resource, not geometry: every primitive needs one through its material input, and assignMaterial applies one to any processed or imported mesh. Every option has a Schemaxis default that is always assigned and read back from the shader, so an empty options object gives a mid-rough, non-metallic blue surface.

Common mistakes and assumptions:

- A material cannot be listed in a scene's visible or meshes; list the mesh that uses it.
- A material that no selected mesh references is pruned and never created, so it is absent from the saved scene.
- Colour values are linear shader values from 0 to 1, not sRGB hex codes; the PNG passes through Blender's colour management.
- Mesh publications (scene meshes) are STL files, which do not carry materials.

Native binding: `material`. Output kind: `["material"]`.

Inputs: none.

| Option | Meaning | Type / constraints | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `colour` | Surface colour and opacity as [red, green, blue, alpha], each 0 to 1. RGB sets the Principled BSDF Base Color (and the viewport display colour); alpha sets the shader Alpha, where 1 is opaque and lower values make the surface see-through in Cycles renders. | `{"type":"array","items":{"type":"number","minimum":0,"maximum":1},"minItems":4,"maxItems":4}` | `[0.1,0.4,0.8,1]` |
| `roughness` | Microfacet roughness of specular reflection and transmission: 0 gives mirror-sharp highlights, 1 broad diffuse ones. Intermediate values give satin finishes; judge the value from test renders. | `{"type":"number","minimum":0,"maximum":1}` | `0.5` |
| `metallic` | Blend between a dielectric (0: diffuse base under a clear specular layer) and a metal (1: fully specular reflection tinted by the base colour, no diffuse). Intermediate values are physically unusual but useful for stylised presentation. | `{"type":"number","minimum":0,"maximum":1}` | `0` |
| `transmission` | Principled BSDF Transmission Weight: 0 is opaque, 1 fully transmissive so light refracts through the surface according to ior, as in glass or liquids. Use it for transparent housings; it makes renders noisier, so raise samples. | `{"type":"number","minimum":0,"maximum":1}` | `0` |
| `coat` | Principled BSDF Coat Weight: strength of a clear lacquer layer on top of the base, as on car paint. Physically it is usually 0 or 1. | `{"type":"number","minimum":0,"maximum":1}` | `0` |
| `coatRoughness` | Roughness of the coat layer only; it matters only when coat is above 0. Low values give a glossy lacquer over a rougher base. | `{"type":"number","minimum":0,"maximum":1}` | `0.03` |
| `emissionColour` | Colour of light emitted by the surface as [red, green, blue], 0 to 1, assigned to Principled BSDF Emission Color (alpha 1). Emission appears only when emissionStrength is above 0. | `{"type":"array","items":{"type":"number","minimum":0,"maximum":1},"minItems":3,"maxItems":3}` | `[0,0,0]` |
| `emissionStrength` | Strength of light emitted by the surface (Principled BSDF Emission Strength). At 1.0 the surface shows its emission colour as if unlit; higher values make it glow and illuminate nearby geometry in Cycles. | `{"type":"number","minimum":0,"maximum":10000}` | `0` |
| `ior` | Index of refraction for specular reflection and transmission. It changes how strongly the surface reflects at normal incidence and, with transmission, how much light bends; 1.5 approximates glass and about 1.33 water. | `{"type":"number","minimum":1,"maximum":4}` | `1.5` |
